name: Gilead
title: Manasse's son and ancestor of the Gileadites
summary: Gilead was the son of Makir and grandson of Manasse, Joseph's son. He became the ancestor of the Gileadite clan, and his descendants were given the land east of the Jordan that came to be known as Gilead. His name is closely linked to both the lineage and the geographical region that played an important role in Israel's history.

keyEvents.title: The Genealogy of Gilead Recorded
keyEvents.description: Gilead is mentioned as the son of Makir, the son of Manasseh, and his descendants are listed as significant clans in Israel.

keyEvents.title: The Descendants of Gilead in the Tribe of Manasseh
keyEvents.description: In 1 Chronicles, the genealogy of Gilead and his place in the tribe of Manasseh is described as an important branch of Joseph's descendants.

keyEvents.title: The Land Allocation to the Descendants of Gilead
keyEvents.description: The region of Gilead east of the Jordan was allotted as an inheritance to the descendants of Makir and Gilead, a decision confirmed under Joshua.

keyEvents.title: The Daughters of Selophahad Claim Their Inheritance
keyEvents.description: Selophahad, a descendant of Gilead through Hefer, had no sons. His daughters claimed their right to inherit before the Lord, and Moses granted them their request.

keyEvents.title: Gilead's Significance in the Period of the Judges
keyEvents.description: The region of Gilead and the Gileadites played a central role during the period of the judges, especially through Jephthah, who was a Gileadite and became a judge in Israel.

keyEvents.title: The Descendants of Gilead in the Land Distribution under Moses
keyEvents.description: Moses allotted the land of Gilead to the descendants of Makir because they were warriors who had conquered the area.
